name: Dehwari
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked (read) LSI Vol X Eranian Family (Grierson 1921, archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.107145): Dehwari section is sociolinguistic notes + specimen, no stress/accent statement; Kieffer refs are wordlist/dialect-geography only.

sources.citation: Sani, Liaquat Ali. 2018. Brahui as native language for a native Dehwari child: a case study of under three-year old child at Ishkina, District Mastung. Balochistan Review 39(2): 61-70.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic case study of Brahui-Dehwari bilingual acquisition with a few Dehwari question/answer pairs; no phonology.

sources.citation: Balochistan Review (University of Balochistan, Quetta), article listings vols. 2010-2022 (347 PDFs), retrieved via the Internet Archive.
sources.note: Only one article in the journal's run names Dehwari (Sani 2018 above); no Dehwari phonology paper exists there.

sources.citation: Spooner, Brian. 'BALUCHISTAN i. Geography, History, and Ethnography' (and any 'DEHWĀR' entry), Encyclopaedia Iranica online.
sources.note: Cited by the Persian Wikipedia article as characterising Dehwari as a Persian variety close to Dari/Tajik; ethnographic, unlikely to give stress, but the standard reference for the identity of the variety.

sources.citation: Bray, Denys. 1934. The Brahui Language, Part II: The Brahui Problem; Part III: Etymological Vocabulary. Delhi: Manager of Publications.
sources.note: Bray, the only trained observer to record Dehwari forms, glosses Dehwari comparanda throughout; if any accent marks on Dehwari words exist in print they would be here (archive.org holds;ernet.dli.2015.283036 'The Brahui Problem Part II-III', not opened today).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1921. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. X: Specimens of Languages of the Eranian Family. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Dehwari', pp. 452-453.
sources.note: Nothing. The 1.5-page section only reprints Bray's 1911-census paragraphs (§282 on the people, §221 on the language: majhul vowels, a>u, b>v, clipped final consonants, vowel shortening, Brahui loans); no accent or stress statement; no specimen with stress marks.

sources.citation: Bray, Denys. 1913. Census of India, 1911. Vol. IV: Baluchistan. Part I: Report. Calcutta. §221 (Persian/Dehwari as vernacular) and §282 (Dehwar), pp. 172-173.
sources.note: Nothing. This is the primary that Grierson quotes; the scanned text (poor quality) contains the same lexical/segmental remarks and no mention of accent or stress in the Dehwari passages.

sources.citation: Wikipedia EN 'Dehwari language'; FA 'گویش دهواری'; FA 'زبان و ادبیات فارسی در بلوچستان'.
sources.note: Nothing; the pages cite only Ethnologue, Glottolog, Sani 2018, Bray 1913 and Spooner's Iranica 'Baluchistan' entry (Dehwari = a Persian variety close to Dari/Tajik).

sources.citation: Jahani, Carina & Agnes Korn (eds.). 2003. The Baloch and Their Neighbours: Ethnic and Linguistic Contact in Balochistan in Historical and Modern Times. Wiesbaden: Reichert.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Google Books snippet shows Dehwari discussed in a dialect-grouping passage; could carry a footnote on Dehwari phonology by Elfenbein or Jahani.

sources.citation: Kieffer, Charles M. 1989. L'avancée du persan vers l'Est: le cas des isolats persanophones les plus orientaux en Afghanistan. Studia Iranica 18(2): 221-236.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Glottolog's only non-colonial reference for dehw1238; per its language code note it cites only individual Dehwari words in a dialect-geography survey of Afghan Persian isolates, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the one modern Iranianist paper touching Dehwari.

sources.citation: Any MPhil/PhD thesis on Dehwari from the University of Balochistan (Persian, Brahui or Linguistics departments) or the HEC Pakistan Research Repository.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only plausible venue for a first-hand phonology of Dehwari; HEC PRR (prr.hec.gov.pk) timed out today and no title could be confirmed, so existence is unverified.
